Let <MATH_0001> be an affine open subscheme which maps into an affine
open <MATH_0002>. We may write <MATH_0003> as a directed limit of affine
schemes <MATH_0004> of finite presentation over <MATH_0005>, see
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0001>.
By assumption, the arrow <MATH_0006> factors as <MATH_0007>
for some <MATH_0008>. After increasing <MATH_0009> we may assume <MATH_0010>
factors through <MATH_0011> as the inverse image of <MATH_0012> in <MATH_0013>
eventually becomes equal to <MATH_0014> by
Limits, Lemma <REF_0002>.
Then the identity morphism <MATH_0015> factors through <MATH_0016> for some <MATH_0017>
in the category of schemes over <MATH_0018>. Thus <MATH_0019> is of finite presentation;
the corresponding algebra fact is that if <MATH_0020> is an <MATH_0021>-algebra
such that <MATH_0022> factors through a finitely presented
<MATH_0023>-algebra, then <MATH_0024> is of finite presentation over <MATH_0025> (nice exercise).
Hence <MATH_0026> is locally of finite presentation over <MATH_0027>.
